faq.title: Frequent Questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions about our clinic and pet care.

vaccinations.title: Vaccinations
vaccinations.q1: When should I start vaccinating my puppy?
vaccinations.a1: Puppies can start vaccinations at 6-8 weeks of age. The first shot is followed by a second one a month later, and a third a month after that. The final shot includes the Rabies vaccine. Afterwards, annual boosters are recommended.
vaccinations.a2: Kittens follow a similar schedule, starting at 6-8 weeks old with three shots spaced a month apart. Annual boosters are recommended thereafter. Full immunity is typically achieved 2-3 weeks after the third vaccination.
vaccinations.q3: Are there side effects to vaccinations?
vaccinations.a3: Side effects are usually mild and temporary. Common ones include reduced appetite, lethargy, or mild swelling at the injection site. Allergic reactions are rare but require immediate veterinary attention.
vaccinations.q4: Is there a vaccine for Leishmaniasis?
vaccinations.a4: Yes. Leishmaniasis is a serious disease transmitted by sandflies. The vaccine reduces symptom severity and makes treatment easier, but it does not prevent infection. Therefore, using repellents (collars/spot-ons) is still necessary.

deworming.title: Deworming & Parasites
deworming.q1: How often should I deworm my pet?
deworming.a1: Intestinal deworming pills should be given every 3 months for both dogs and cats. Puppies and kittens require more frequent doses.
deworming.a2: Heartworm (Dirofilaria) is transmitted by mosquitoes. Prevention for dogs involves a monthly pill (killing larvae) and a repellent (collar/spot-on). For cats, monthly prevention is also available.
deworming.q3: How do I protect my dog from fleas and ticks?
deworming.a3: Effective protection relies on a combination of products. For dogs, we recommend a spot-on or pill (killing fleas/ticks) combined with a collar (repelling sandflies/mosquitoes).
deworming.q4: Can I use dog products on my cat?
deworming.a4: NO! Never use a dog product on a cat or vice versa without consulting a veterinarian. Some ingredients safe for dogs are toxic to cats.

nutrition.title: Nutrition
nutrition.q1: What is the best diet for my pet?
nutrition.a1: The main diet should be high-quality dry food (kibble) suitable for their life stage (junior, adult, senior) and breed size. Canned food can be used as a supplement or treat.
nutrition.a2: Yes, treats can be used for training or as a supplement to the diet, but moderation is key.
nutrition.q3: Can I give bones to my dog?
nutrition.a3: NO! Bones can cause gastrointestinal upset or, worse, obstruction which may require surgery and can be life-threatening.
nutrition.q4: Is human food safe for pets?
nutrition.a4: Generally, no. Human food is unbalanced and may contain toxic ingredients like onions, raisins, or chocolate. Pets can also become picky eaters if fed human food often.

bad_breath.title: Bad Breath
bad_breath.q1: Why does my pet have bad breath?
bad_breath.a1: Bad breath is usually caused by tartar and gingivitis. Professional dental cleaning at the clinic is the required treatment. Regular brushing helps prevent it.

grooming.title: Grooming & Bathing
grooming.q1: How often should I bathe my pet?
grooming.a1: Bathing is typically not needed more than once a month unless there is a specific skin condition. Always use a pet-specific shampoo and avoid getting water in the ears.
grooming.a2: Haircuts are not strictly necessary but can help dogs in summer or remove mats/knots. There is no restriction on frequency.
